title: The One Role Gen Z Women Still Want Men To Play (HTML <title>: "What Gen Z Men and Women Want Most in a Partner")
author: Wendy Wang (Director of Research, Institute for Family Studies); interactive charts by Ken Burchfiel
publication: Institute for Family Studies (ifstudies.org) blog — reporting the IFS/YouGov Gen-Z survey
accessedVia: Claude Browser pane (preview_start + get_page_text) on 2026-07-29. WebFetch REFUSED verbatim reproduction and returned only a paraphrase, so the browser route was required. The appended numeric block was read from the report's own Plotly appendix iframe at https://ifstudies.org/ifs-admin/resources/html_iframe/interactive_partyid_charts.html by reading the graph divs' .data trace arrays while cycling the page's own <select> controls.
notes: PRIMARY for FIGURE 1. Excerpt capture, not a full-text mirror: every sentence carrying a number, subgroup label, question frame, or methodology statement is byte-verbatim and in order; purely discursive passages are elided and marked [...]. Original typos preserved ("IFS/Gov survey", "striking patten", "Previous researchshows", "weighed" for "weighted"). Survey sponsor is IFS/YouGov ALONE — AEI is NOT a sponsor of this instrument. Field dates April 7-15, 2025; n=2,000 men + 1,000 women ages 18-29 (total 3,000); YouGov opt-in panel MATCHED to a modeled frame and propensity-weighted — NOT a probability sample, and NO margin of error is published. The appended trace values are the report's own published numbers at full precision and are the decisive evidence that the 36% figure belongs to CONSERVATIVE WOMEN (36.392) and not to conservative men (36.979).

title: NATIONAL ELECTION POOL EXIT POLL METHODS STATEMENT (November 5, 2024)
author: Edison Research (questionnaire prepared by NEP members ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC)
publication: National Election Pool, hosted by ABC News
accessedVia: WebFetch returned the file as unreadable binary but saved it locally; text extracted with PyMuPDF (fitz) via Bash on 2026-07-29. 1 page, native text layer, no OCR.
notes: PRIMARY for FIGURE 2's METHODOLOGY. Reproduced in full, byte-verbatim (one U+FFFD encoding artifact preserved and flagged). This is the instrument's own methods document. It is the source of the exit poll's design facts: 279 Election Day polling places, 27 early in-person locations in only 4 states (GA, NV, NC, OH), plus a Registration-Based-Sample multi-mode poll of absentee/early voters fielded Oct 24 - Nov 2 (i.e. BEFORE Election Day, among people who said they have voted or definitely will). It publishes NO single national margin of error — only a table of typical sampling error by subgroup base size — and it publishes no base n for an 18-29-by-gender crossbreak, which is why no MOE can be honestly quoted for the young-men-vs-young-women figures. Its own caveat: "Other nonsampling factors, including nonresponse, are likely to increase the total error."
